name: maximize_sign
description: clingo rewrites #maximize{w@l,t : b} into #minimize{-w@l,t : b}, so a maximized element pays the opposite of the weight written down. Taking items 1 and 3 is worth 5+4, which clingo reports as an optimization value of -9; reporting +9 instead would also invert the comparison used to explain optimality.
program:
v(1,5).
v(2,3).
v(3,4).
{take(X)} :- v(X,_).
:- #count{X : take(X)} > 2.
#maximize{ W@1,X : take(X), v(X,W) }.
